items.label: Consumer sentiment (University of Michigan)
items.value_label: 48.0, October final (Oct 23), revised up from the 46.3 preliminary
items.say: Still among the lowest readings in the survey's history; the final October figure was revised up to nearly September's level.
items.src: Trading Economics calendar (University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers), Oct 23

items.label: Gasoline, national average (AAA)
items.value_label: $4.169 a gallon (Nov 2; AAA's page still showed Nov 2 on the morning of Nov 3)
items.compare: $3.036 a year ago; $4.286 a week ago; $4.396 a month ago
items.say: Up about 37% in a year, though 12 cents lower than a week ago and 23 cents below a month ago.

items.label: A Chipotle chicken burrito bowl
items.say: Roughly 15–20% more than four years ago; restaurant prices overall are up 3.4% in the past year (CPI food away from home, August).
items.src: Reuters via ThePricer (May 2026); Food Business News (Oct 2022)

items.label: Prediction markets: Democratic House
items.compare: Senate: about 74% Democratic from the balance-of-power contracts (Democrats win both 73.5¢ on Kalshi and 74.5¢ on Polymarket; Democratic House with Republican Senate 19.5¢ and 18.5¢; Republican House with Democratic Senate about 0.5¢; Republicans win both 5.9¢ and 4.5¢)
items.say: Markets ended the campaign at their most Democratic: the House price is steady at about 94 and the Senate up a point or two since Nov 2 to about 74.
items.src: DeFi Rate, Nov 2 (7:04 p.m. ET), checked Nov 3

items.label: Cook Political Report House ratings
items.value_label: 18 toss-ups in Cook's last House table (Oct 30); final Senate ratings Nov 2 move Michigan to Lean D and leave six toss-ups
items.compare: Cook's projection (Oct 30): Democrats flip 12-25 seats, up to 240; its final Senate ratings (Nov 2) move Michigan from Toss Up to Lean D, leaving Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Ohio and Texas as toss-ups. Sabato's Crystal Ball's final ratings (Nov 2): House 239 at least Lean D to 196 at least Lean R after the last toss-ups broke 14-3 to Lean D; Senate 53-47 with no toss-ups; governors 28-22, with Georgia and Nevada to Lean D, Alaska to Likely D and New Hampshire to Lean R. Inside Elections' final ratings (Oct 31): Democrats gain 20-30 House seats and 4-6 Senate seats
items.say: All three raters finished with Democrats favored for both chambers; Sabato's final map has no Senate toss-ups and Cook's has six.
items.src: Cook Political Report, Oct 30 and Nov 2 (via FiftyPlusOne, Nov 3); Sabato's Crystal Ball, Nov 2; Inside Elections (Roll Call), Oct 31

items.label: House members not seeking re-election
items.value_label: 36 Republicans, 24 Democrats (plus two Democratic delegates); 29 are running for other office
items.say: More Republicans leaving, including 20 running for other office; retirements have not tracked the swing in past midterms.
